summary: Defines new media types so the CoAP FETCH, PATCH and iPATCH methods can work with Sensor Measurement Lists (SenML) data. This allows parts of sensor data or settings to be read or updated in one request.

eli5.summary: Instead of replacing a whole notebook, you can read or fix a single line. This lets tiny devices do that with sensor data.

questions: how to patch senml data with coap
what media types are used for senml fetch
what are the senml-etch media types
what happens when a senml patch is invalid
subtitle: Two new media types let constrained devices read or change just part of a SenML sensor data pack.

tldr.problem: SenML packs can hold many sensor readings or settings, but a client often wants only some of the records, or wants to change a few of them, without sending the whole pack.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines the media types application/senml-etch+json and application/senml-etch+cbor. With them, a CoAP FETCH request selects matching records by name, time and unit, and PATCH or iPATCH changes, adds or removes records.
tldr.outcome: Partial reads and updates of SenML data work with existing SenML parsers, and a patch is applied entirely or not at all.

today: RFC 8790 is a Proposed Standard and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It builds on RFC 8428 and RFC 8132.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
Sensor Measurement Lists (SenML) is a media type and data model for sending collections of resources, such as batches of sensor data or configuration parameters. The CoAP FETCH, PATCH and iPATCH methods access and update parts of a resource, or several resources, with one request.

This RFC defines two new media types for using those methods with SenML data: one based on JSON and one based on CBOR. They also work for Sensor Streaming Measurement Lists (SenSML) data. The text writes (i)PATCH when PATCH and iPATCH behave the same, which they do here.

The running example is a pack of three records for a dimmable light, sharing the base name 2001:db8::2/3311/0/, with names 5850 (a boolean), 5851 (a number, 42) and 5750 (a string, "Ceiling light").
sections.eli5: A SenML pack is like a list of sensor readings. This RFC gives us ways to ask for part of the list or to change part of it.

sections.title: Fetch and Patch Packs
sections.content:
The RFC adds some terms. A Fetch Record is a set of parameters used to match SenML records, and a Fetch Pack is one or more of them in an array. A Patch Record is similar but also carries instructions for changing existing packs, and a Patch Pack is an array of them. A Target Record is a record that matches the selection, and a Target Pack is the pack being fetched from or patched.

The new media types are modeled as extensions of SenML so existing parsers and generators, especially on constrained devices, can be reused. Unless stated otherwise, Fetch and Patch Packs follow the same rules as SenML packs. The key differences are that a null value can remove records in a patch, Fetch Records have no value fields, and Fetch and Patch Records have no default time or base version when those fields are omitted.
sections.eli5: A fetch pack is a shopping list of what to look up. A patch pack is a list of corrections to make.

sections.title: SenML FETCH
sections.content:
FETCH selects and returns a subset of the records, in sequence, from one or more SenML packs. Records are selected by names, given with the SenML name and/or base name fields. They are matched after resolving, which means joining the base name and the name as RFC 8428 defines. A Fetch Pack MUST contain at least one Fetch Record, and each Fetch Record MUST contain a name and/or base name.

Time and unit can narrow the match. If a Fetch Record gives no time or unit, all records with that name match, so a missing time does not mean zero as it does in ordinary SenML. If a time is given, a target matches only when its resolved time and name are equal. The same holds for units, and if both are given, both must match. Each Target Record appears in the response at most once. If nothing matches, the response is an empty pack.

Fetch Records MUST NOT contain fields other than name, base name, time, base time, unit and base unit. Implementations MUST reject a Fetch Pack with other fields and generate an error, for example the 4.22 (Unprocessable Entity) CoAP response code.
sections.eli5: You tell the device which names you want, and it hands back only those readings. If you also name a time or a unit, it hands back only the ones that match those too.

sections.title: SenML (i)PATCH
sections.content:
(i)PATCH can change fields of records, add new records and remove existing ones. Names, times and units are matched as in FETCH, except each Patch Record MUST match at most one Target Record, because matching several would create multiple copies of the same record. Applying Patch Packs is idempotent, so PATCH and iPATCH are equivalent for SenML. All Patch Records MUST contain at least a SenML Value or Sum field.

When the name matches an existing record and the resolved time and unit either do not exist in both or are equal, the target record is replaced by the contents of the Patch Record. If no existing record matches, the Patch Record is added to the pack. If a Patch Record has a value (v) of null, it is not added, and the matched record, if any, is removed.

Patch Records MUST be applied in the order they appear. If several Patch Packs are processed at once, the result MUST be equivalent to applying them in one sequence. An invalid Patch Pack MUST be rejected with an error, and then the target pack is unchanged, so either all or none of the records are applied. RFC 8132 suggests codes such as 4.22 (Unprocessable Entity) and 4.09 (Conflict).
sections.eli5: A patch changes the readings you name, adds ones that were missing and erases ones you mark as null. It is all or nothing: if one correction is bad, none of them are applied.

sections.title: Fragments and Extensibility
sections.content:
Fragment identification works as in SenML JSON and CBOR. The rec scheme is followed by a comma-separated list of record positions or ranges. For example, rec=3,5 selects the 3rd and 5th record of a Fetch or Patch Pack.

SenML's mandatory-to-understand field mechanism does not apply to Patch Packs. Unknown fields MUST NOT cause an error and are treated like any other field, for example added to target records. Only a small subset of SenML fields is allowed in Fetch Records, but future specifications may allow new fields there and new fields for selecting patch targets.
sections.eli5: If a patch contains a field the device has never heard of, it just keeps it with the record instead of complaining.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The security and privacy considerations of SenML also apply, and CoAP's security mechanisms protect the FETCH and (i)PATCH methods.

Because a client can pass arbitrary names to the target resource, the resource implementer must only allow access to names that are really part of, or reachable through, that resource. The receiver must make sure that input does not lead to uncontrolled special interpretation by the system. If the client is not allowed to GET or PUT the full target resource, access control rules must be evaluated for each record in the pack.
sections.eli5: Because you can ask for any name, the device has to check each request. Someone allowed to read only the light must not get the door lock.

sections.title: Media Types and Content-Format IDs
sections.content: IANA registered two media types and CoAP Content-Format IDs: application/senml-etch+json with ID 320 and application/senml-etch+cbor with ID 322. Both are intended for common usage, and the change controller is the IESG. The registered file extensions are senml-etchj and senml-etchc.
sections.eli5: The two new formats got official names and numbers so devices can tell them apart.
